historical_reviews.deepseek: Useful observations are present, but they do not prove data integrity or a completed mirror rebuild and do not exclude OS/production arrays.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly adds topology and destructive-data safeguards.
historical_reviews.history: No exact-code V3.1 record was found.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Requires RAID1-specific proof that degraded writes are later mirrored: compare the post-degraded-write corpus only after resynchronization, not merely the original pre-pull hashes.

original_test_intent: Verify that an isolated RAID1 stays accessible during single-member hot removal, accepts bounded degraded-mode file operations, reintegrates the same member, fully resynchronizes, and preserves both preexisting and degraded-period data across five cycles per member.
original_method: Bind array UUID, RAID implementation and member serial/WWN-to-bay map; create a disposable corpus; have an operator remove one approved mirror member; perform bounded degraded reads/writes; reinsert the exact member; wait for verified resync; compare the full post-write corpus and health before the next cycle.
manual_activity: Operator removes/reinserts the exact labeled mirror member only after automation verifies array UUID, member serial/WWN, bay and degraded-operation authorization.
safety_requirements: Never guess array, member or bay
Stop on second-member, filesystem, I/O or controller anomaly
Do not start next cycle before full resync and scrub/health checks
Do not mistake spare activation for original-member recovery
agent_execution_scope: Inventory array UUID, level, implementation and member identities
Verify safe isolated targets and synchronized baseline
Monitor degraded state and kernel/controller events
Perform only approved bounded degraded file operations
Verify exact member return and resync progress
Hash complete preexisting and degraded-write corpus
Record every member/cycle and report without final verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Enumeration, dmesg and RAID state are necessary but insufficient: the plan must select the actual mdadm or controller stack, validate array/member identity, perform the mandated file operations, and prove full resync plus post-degraded-write integrity.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: For each mirror member and five cycles, verify synchronized RAID1, pull the mapped member, confirm degraded access, perform approved corpus mutations, reinsert the same member, wait for complete resync, then validate all hashes, array metadata and member health.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: RAID1, one-member removal, degraded copy/delete, reinsertion, lsblk/nvme visibility, MD5, all members, five cycles and 40/20-minute timing are preserved; targets and controller stack are not guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use an array/member cycle ledger with array UUID, event count, degraded write-set manifest, resync start/end, bitmap/journal state, final hashes and media health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Proves that data written while degraded is actually mirrored after recovery, not just that old files remain readable.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Detects wrong member/bay, stale mirror recovery, incomplete resync, filesystem damage and silent content divergence.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: RAID1 tolerates one member loss but offers no redundancy during the degraded window; latent errors on the survivor can make recovery fail.

project_override_considerations: The source mentions both lsblk/nvme and mdadm/storcli possibilities. The exact RAID implementation and controller path must be identified; the private software-RAID script cannot be assumed applicable to hardware RAID.
expected_evidence: No hardware PASS claim by the agent

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently targets RAID1 single-member hot-plug, degraded access and recovery. Tool choice depends on actual implementation but does not conflict with the purpose.

blocked_analysis.analysis: A disposable array, exact topology and recovery can be supplied. Unknown/production targets or lack of safe recovery after request would block execution.

review_improvement: Makes the mirror-specific degraded-write and resynchronization behavior testable and prevents generic enumeration from passing an unsafe or incomplete RAID1 recovery.
independent_technical_reasoning: RAID1 accessibility while degraded does not prove recovery correctness. New and modified blocks written during the degraded interval must be propagated to the returning member, so resync completion and a post-resync corpus hash are essential. Because member handling is manual and writes affect an array, exact topology and approval make this REQUIRES.
